context.body: Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Hushai greets Absalom, explains his allegiance, and Ahithophel counsels public possession of David’s concubines on the roof.
observations.label: Absalom enters Jerusalem and receives Ahithophel’s counsel: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Absalom, Hushai, Ahithophel, Israel, and David’s concubines, Jerusalem and the palace roof, entering, testing allegiance, advising, pitching a tent, and going publicly to the concubines visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Absalom enters Jerusalem and receives Ahithophel’s counsel: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Absalom, Hushai, Ahithophel, Israel, and David’s concubines · Jerusalem and the palace roof · entering, testing allegiance, advising, pitching a tent, and going publicly to the concubines · the seized city displays a household consequence Nathan had announced

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 16:15–23 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the seized city displays a household consequence Nathan had announced inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
